materials.title: Mike Tyson once said ... What’s a real-life example of someone learning that lesson?
verified_claims: The thread was visible on r/AskReddit's Top/This Month listing.
The opened public detail page displayed 22K votes and 2.9K comments.
The title frames a discussion about online disrespect and real-world consequences.
limits: Votes and comments are approximate UI displays captured at the observation time.
Comments are user-generated anecdotes and were not treated as independently verified facts.
The Mike Tyson attribution appears in the post title and was not independently verified in this round.
materials.rights: Public page read for editorial research; no bulk collection or comment corpus downloaded.

verified_claims: The official page is dated 2025-02-20 and reports 2024 prosecutorial/public-interest work.
For 2024 January–November, procuratorates filed 11,463 public-interest litigation matters involving minors.
The page identifies areas including food around schools, minors’ personal information, and internet cafes admitting minors.
limits: The 11,463 figure is filings, not number of victims, crimes, convictions, or every confirmed violation.

materials.title: Observation Moderates the Moral Licensing Effect: A Meta-Analytic Test of Interpersonal and Intrapsychic Mechanisms
verified_claims: PubMed metadata identifies the 2025 paper and its authors.
The abstract reports a meta-analysis of 115 experiments involving 21,770 participants.

The abstract reports stronger licensing when participants were observed (g=0.65) than unobserved (g=0.13), with publication-bias-adjusted support in observed conditions and near-zero effect when unobserved.
limits: The source is a meta-analysis of experimental studies, not a universal rule about every public good deed.
The everyday examples in C222 are editorial interpretation; they are not participant-level findings from this abstract.
materials.rights: Public PubMed abstract read for editorial research; no bulk collection.
